songLine: Nine-Eleven Trillions: Follow the Kayfabe-Money! Official narrative, torn in half.
reason: '9/11' in the title would be read as 'nine slash eleven' or a date; spoken as 'Nine-Eleven'. Lore's meta-reference to Uncle FrizzleBob dropped so he appears only once (card 60); the POWER (discard the Official Narrative) becomes the satirical tag, matching the torn-dollar motif.

songLine: Nose down: Rule Number One: Follow the Money. A crime has perpetrators.
reason: '#1' is unspeakable; 'Rule Number One' (also reused as the callback in card 28).

songLine: Peekaboo: Treasury's Ten Veils. You never reach my source.
reason: Numeral '10' written out as 'Ten' for clean delivery.

songLine: Easy now: The Fourteen Million Bridge. Billions, balanced on a matchstick.
reason: '$14' would be read as 'dollar fourteen'; written out as 'Fourteen Million'.

songLine: The Secret Eighty Percent Kickback: equity back, billions and counting.
reason: '80%' written out as 'Eighty Percent'.

songLine: Floors Ninety-Three to a Hundred: impact zone. Two thousand employees. And the data.
reason: '93 To 100' written out as 'Ninety-Three to a Hundred'.

songLine: The Ten Million Anomalies: phantom orders, hardware nobody needed.
reason: '$10M' is unpronounceable as printed; 'Ten Million'.

songLine: The Upper West Side Safehouse: he buried the inquiry from home. The investigators never came back.
reason: Lore compressed for tempo: 'IT staff investigating the fraud perished in the conference call' rendered as 'The investigators never came back' - humane, no mechanics, keeps the executive as the target.

songLine: Tick, tock: The Forty-Minute Window. Bank mainframes, taken over. Download. Purge.
reason: '40-Minute' written out as 'Forty-Minute'.

songLine: Records, please? The C-B-O-E Shredder. Destroyed.
reason: Acronym 'CBOE' spelled 'C-B-O-E' so Suno does not sing 'see-bo'. Same in card 59.

songLine: All rise: The S-E-C Investigation. Insiders didn't trade. So who knew?
reason: Acronym 'SEC' spelled 'S-E-C' so it is not read as the word 'sec'. Same in card 52.

songLine: Final word: The Nine-Eleven Commission Handwave. Rule Number One? Of little practical significance.
reason: '9/11' spoken as 'Nine-Eleven'.

songLine: P-Tech Enterprise Architecture: God's eye view. Foresee problems, or cause them.
reason: 'Ptech' rendered 'P-Tech' for pronunciation; applies to every Ptech mention in the song (cards 29 and 35).

songLine: The F-A-A Basement Interoperability: hunting holes in the hijack response.
reason: Acronym 'FAA' spelled 'F-A-A'.

songLine: Ka-chunk: Tom Ridge's Rubber Stamp. In no way a security risk.
reason: Ridge quote '"in no way jeopardizes the security of the country"' compressed to 'In no way a security risk' to fit the 5000-character limit; meaning unchanged.

songLine: The Two-Point-Three Trillion Cushion: eight thousand per American.
reason: '$2.3 Trillion' written out as 'Two-Point-Three Trillion'.

songLine: Wedge One Renovations: the budget office just moved back in. Thirty-four bookkeepers and analysts killed.
reason: 'Wedge 1' written out as 'Wedge One'.

songLine: Building Seven S-E-C Vault: the Enron files, gone with the building.
reason: 'Building 7 SEC' written out as 'Building Seven S-E-C'.

songLine: Snowball! The Eight-Point-Five Trillion Benchmark. Great success at losing money.
reason: '$8.5 Trillion' written out as 'Eight-Point-Five Trillion'.

songLine: Uncle FrizzleBob's Verdict: Nine-Eleven changed everything. It made the house infinitely rich. Follow the Kayfabe-Money, kids!
reason: Quote trimmed for tempo ('They told you 9/11 changed everything. They were right:' becomes 'Nine-Eleven changed everything.'); the 'house infinitely rich' payoff and closing 'Follow the Kayfabe-Money, kids!' are kept verbatim.
